messages.subject: Detection Probability of 1
messages.body_plain:
Dear List Members,

I'm encountering some problems in a data set I'm currently analyzing, nam=
ely that Distance is not fitting a curve to the data. My analysis continu=
es to output a probability of detection of 1.0000, and all of my detectio=
n probability plots appear as straight lines. I'm wondering what might ca=
use this to happen? I'm not getting any error messages in this analysis t=
hat I haven't seen before in other successful analyses. I can send screen=

 shots of the output and my data text file if this would be helpful.

Thank you for the help,
Kelly O'Connor

messages.subject: Overlapped transects
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,
I have a question about survey designs. I designed a survey laying

transects 3 km apart each other. Once I finished the survey I discovered

with a GIS software that in fact some transects were separated a bit less

than the 3 km predefined distance, so areas searched (outer distances)
overlapped 10-20%. Some of these transects were searched within the same

day while others were separated in time (2-3 days). Do I have to consider
those transects overlapped as one sampling unit (summing effort and
observations in one transect?
Thanks in advance
Alejandro

--

messages.subject: Re: Overlapped transects
messages.body_plain:
Alejandro, while this violates the independence assumption, the implication=
s of such overlap are minor.  Variance estimates are robust to this effect.=
  For an illustration of this for point transect sampling, see=20
Buckland, S.T. 2006.  Point transect surveys for songbirds:  robust methodo=
logies.  The Auk 123, 345-357.
I'll send you a copy of this off-list.

Steve Buckland

messages.subject: Post stratification
messages.body_plain:
Hello,

I am a program Distance beginner and have a question regarding how effort=
 and sample size are calculated during the post-stratification process.=20=

I have bird surveys from 7 forest strata across 4 years. Each site was vi=
sited 2 times per year. I imported my data with 7 regional stratum, sites=
 (153) and effort (8) at the point level, and species, distance, observer=
, and stratum+year and the observation level. I am interested in post-str=
atifying to determine how densities vary among the 7 strata across each o=
f the 4 years. This generates 28 different density estimates.=20

When I run the model it shows that I have 4,284 samples and that effort i=
s 33, 824 (It appears to have multiplied my actual effort and sample size=
 by my number of post-stratification levels (28). Should not the sample s=
ize and effort remain consistent? If so, what might be the source of erro=
r?=20

Thank you for your time, E.M.

--

messages.subject: Re: Post stratification
messages.body_plain:
E.M.

Yes, I can duplicate what you report regarding the summary statistics in
the Distance output regarding the multiplication of number of sites and
number of total visits by the number of post-stratification visits.  But
I believe the calculations of density/abundance are computed correctly.

If you do one or two hand calculations [D=(n*h(0))/(2*k*pi)] to check
that you are getting the correct densities for your stratum/year
combinations.  Let me know if your hand calculations match the output.
